description: The four-level tree on the left has no value labels. Its first three levels are full, with 1, 2, and 4 nodes. From left to right on the third level, the first two nodes each have both a left and a right child, the third has only a left child, and the fourth has no children. The five leaves on the fourth level therefore occupy the five leftmost positions consecutively.

The heading on the right reads “Complete binary tree.” Beneath the tree, a long arrow points left. A gray note below the arrow reads “The bottom level fills from the left. All other levels are full.” Nodes on the bottom level must occupy consecutive positions starting at the far left, with no gaps.

frames.explanation: The tree has height 3 and 12 nodes and satisfies the definition of a complete binary tree. It is not perfect because three positions on the right of the fourth level are empty.
frames.title: Complete binary tree: the last level fills consecutively from the left

summary: The first three levels are full. The fourth level occupies five consecutive positions starting at the left, leaving only its three rightmost positions empty.
title: Complete binary tree: the last level fills consecutively from the left
